data.title: Webhook
data.tagline: A mechanism where the other party proactively notifies an address you configured when something happens
data.learningOutcome: Facing when A happens, do B, you can say whether to use a webhook or poll on a schedule.
data.description: After an event such as a payment, a platform can attempt to deliver an HTTP request to your configured endpoint. Delivery may be delayed, fail, be retried, duplicate, or arrive out of order. Verify the source, deduplicate events, and read back the business record; polling can provide a reconciliation fallback.

learning.assumes: You have seen a when A happens, do B requirement, or polling for new data.
learning.outcome: Facing when A happens, do B, you can say whether to use a webhook or poll on a schedule.

distinctions.label: Polling
distinctions.explanation: Polling means you ask periodically; a webhook is the other party attempting to push an event. Either may have delay, and a webhook is not guaranteed to arrive at the moment the event occurs.

distinctions.label: Ordinary API
distinctions.explanation: An ordinary API is you actively requesting the other party; a webhook is the other party actively hitting your configured address—the direction is reversed.

explanation.title: Notified when it happens
explanation.text: The platform may attempt delivery after an event; timing can vary, and retries or duplicate events are possible.

explanation.title: Your service processes on receipt
explanation.text: On receipt, verify the source and content, then update the order or access state according to the business flow. Acknowledge receipt as the provider expects and read back the business record to verify.

explanation.title: Guard against duplicates and forgery
explanation.text: Notifications may be delayed, fail, be retried, duplicate, or arrive out of order; provider retries still do not guarantee delivery. Verify signatures, deduplicate, and reconcile critical records.

data.boundary: A webhook does not guarantee delivery: network trouble or temporary downtime can make an attempt fail. Follow the provider's retry policy and reconcile critical business records; do not assume every event will arrive.

lessonPractice.title: The payment platform offers event notifications. Which approach lets it notify your server after a payment?

options.label: Register a webhook receiver and wait for the platform to send events
options.feedback: Correct. The platform attempts event delivery without repeated polling, but arrival time can vary. Verify the source and handle duplicate events safely.

options.label: Check the payment platform's order status every minute
options.feedback: Here your service initiates scheduled queries; the platform is not sending an event notification.

options.label: Have users contact us after paying to unlock manually
options.feedback: This relies on the customer and a person passing on the message, rather than the platform notifying your server automatically.

data.agentPrompt: Integrate a webhook for successful payments: configure the receiving address, verify the signature and order number on notification, then unlock membership. Duplicate notifications for the same order must not unlock twice; acknowledge receipt according to the provider's requirements and verify the final order state.
